The seccomp-bpf filter is **x86_64-linux-only** by design: it's compiled for `AUDIT_ARCH_X86_64`, and the `syscall_nr` table (`crates/lightr-engine/src/engine/seccomp/syscalls.rs`) resolves names via x86_64 `libc::SYS_*` constants — many of which (`SYS_access`, `SYS_arch_prctl`, `SYS_chmod`, `SYS_chown`, `SYS_creat`, `SYS_dup2`, `SYS_epoll_create`, `SYS_epoll_ctl_old`, …) do not exist on `aarch64` (that arch dropped the legacy syscalls; `arch_prctl` is x86-specific).

This surfaced as a hard **`aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu` release build failure** (`error[E0425]: cannot find value SYS_* in crate libc`) in the `v0.1.0` release run: https://github.com/HumanGuardrail/hugr-lightr/actions/runs/28616984682

**Current behavior (shipped):** the seccomp module is `#[cfg(all(target_os="linux", target_arch="x86_64"))]`-gated, so on non-x86_64 linux `--seccomp <path>` and `--seccomp default` **fail closed** — honest exit 2 at the CLI (`seccomp_arch_policy`), `_exit` in PID 1 as defense-in-depth — never a silent unfiltered run. No `--seccomp` flag = runs without a filter, same as x86_64 without the flag. Truth ledger scoped accordingly (parity-audit F-204, #111).

**This issue:** add a per-arch syscall-number table (at minimum aarch64: `AUDIT_ARCH_AARCH64` + the aarch64 `SYS_*` set) so the seccomp filter compiles + enforces on aarch64-linux too, then flip the arch-gate to include it. A `const`-generic or a `#[cfg(target_arch)]` table keyed on the target's `AUDIT_ARCH_*` is the natural shape. Add an aarch64 differential to the `security-flags` CI job once a runner is available.
title: aarch64 seccomp support (per-arch syscall table)

## Confirmed blocker for PR #169 — no qualified correction yet

Source `2cfd7bf84c90161cff7e64b9705f3afa2b785c84`, tested merge `af3a98b4412e5fc5c05df00d996d733b804e0e97`, tree `d42aed2806993ffb4f63884b7ea54872741cdad4`. Full CI [35415473360](https://github.com/gmhelmold/hugr-lightr/actions/runs/35415473360) failed current macOS ARM job **105823167301**, macOS 26.6.2 arm64. The native Windows gate and six complementary workflows passed, but they do not waive this failure. Parent #146 and integration remain at 2b91281; #169 must not merge until the corrected candidate is qualified.

### Original remote observation

`cargo test --workspace --features vz --lib --bins -- --skip gc_reclaims_hard_killed_run_dir`, pinned Rust 1.96.0, denied warnings and the repository Swift rpath:

```text
---- stream::tests::open_exec_tty_uses_pty_master_no_stderr stdout ----
thread 'stream::tests::open_exec_tty_uses_pty_master_no_stderr' (29744)
panicked at crates/lightr-cri-backend/src/stream_tests.rs:173:10:
pty stream failed before a complete line: Kind(UnexpectedEof)

test result: FAILED. 23 passed; 1 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out
```

The original echo command and assertions have not been changed. This is not a Windows-link-planner failure, but it is a real required-CI blocker.

### New native evidence and mechanism

Two disposable PTY pairs on the owner's Intel Mac, macOS 15.3.2: writing `pty-drain-witness\n`, closing the final slave, then reading the master returned an empty byte string. Keeping the slave open returned the exact native `pty-drain-witness\r\n`. A separate `/bin/echo hello-tty` observation held a slave in a per-child worker, reported process exit 0 before the first read, drained the terminal, then closed: master yielded `hello-tty\r\n` and then EOF. These observations support a lifecycle mechanism; they are not a recovered stack of the remote failure or a qualified production implementation.

`open_exec_tty` stores the slave handles in its Command, spawns the child, and returns the master handles. The Command's destructor drops its slave handles at function return. If the fast child has already exited, the last close occurs before the caller can consume the master. Apple's [ptsclose](https://github.com/apple-oss-distributions/xnu/blob/main/bsd/kern/tty_dev.c) and [ttyclose](https://github.com/apple-oss-distributions/xnu/blob/main/bsd/kern/tty.c) implementations include final-close queue flushing; this source reference is not an assertion that the checked-in main branch is the exact runner kernel.

### Regression executed against unchanged production code

Added two local, scoped native regression methods. The first deliberately waits for the real echo process to exit before reading, without a sleep, serialization workaround or retry. It compiled and failed with Cargo child exit **101**:

```text
stream::tests::pty_lifetime::pty_exec_exit_before_first_read_preserves_the_complete_line ... FAILED
exited PTY child lost its queued output: Kind(UnexpectedEof)
test result: FAILED. 0 passed; 1 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 25 filtered out
```

The second method checks the opposite ordering: the stream must reach its terminal state without requiring the caller to consume ExitWaiter first. It was compiled in that executable but was not selected/executed in this before run. Neither method replaces the original test.

Evidence is outside the repository in `/tmp/lightr-winlink-publish-0v8wt7sl`:
- `pty-before.log` SHA256 `8aeaecb93ba01fbe1bfbce581131dffef6190af7bdcf4b0c2542c8f183f7e4c0`.
- `pty-close-observation.json` SHA256 `04a1f9fef3dff3085ae2be11a465eb2929c96300f1863a2a55dba5e398bf3c08`.
- `pty-drain-order-observation.json` SHA256 `ee462593b78d7144089270087291466a3768f49244982a0aa7992ca7fbb1a5f5`.
- Regression source SHA256 `f0e8189dca512a7739adf9323fee2c1fdf50812199797ce39c84a21496093d10`.

A command proposing the production lifetime repair was blocked by execution security before running. Read-back confirmed stream.rs byte-identical to published HEAD and no stream_pty.rs created. No alternative route was used to apply that refused change. Thus there is no after-fix Rust result or repair commit yet. The published Windows planner remains intact.

## Five acceptance groups

**Success criteria:** the real fast child retains complete terminal output even when its exit is observed before the first read. Terminal EOF/hangup remains observable when output is drained before the waiter is consumed. Report the real exit code without treating it as proof of successful output delivery.

**Completeness criteria:** preserve the original echo test and both orderings; check client disconnect, child/setup failures, output-drain failures, worker/handle cleanup and relevant native Unix profiles. Explain the lifetime of any retained slave, and do not create a dependency cycle between reading and waiting.

**Quality standards:** minimal separately attributable repair, pinned Rust 1.96.0, denied warnings, formatting, original assertions and all CI jobs retained. No sleep-length increase, retry-until-green, skip, fixture substitution or capability/protection bypass. Additional platform code must receive line-level review.

**Invariants:** raw streaming vocabulary unchanged unless explicitly ratified; process exit and stream completion are distinct facts. No arbitrary-process signalling, orphaned setup child, unbounded output buffer or permanent daemon. Do not conceal native I/O errors or claim arbitrary descendant supervision from a direct-child fix.

**Definition of Done:** before/after regression tied to the mechanism, full corrected-head CI and complementary gates pass, original and added tests present in native logs, labeled coordinator self-review, reviewed expected-head integration, fresh parent #146 CI verified, and only owned branch/worktree/build resources retired. Closing this blocker does not close #147/#152 or authorize main/protocol activation.

### Scope

`DestinationAnchor::prepare_tree(TreePlan, NameProbeLimits, Wait)` runs the accepted actual-destination whole-tree name probe first, then prepares the persistent operation-owned namespace directly below the retained destination root. Directories use descriptor-relative create-only mkdirat + no-follow acquisition; regular files use O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW|O_CLOEXEC and are retained internally; POSIX links use symlinkat with exact stored UTF-8 target text.

The prepared tree revalidates every owned binding and enumerates the retained root plus each created directory through fresh directory descriptions to require the exact planned child count. A foreign unplanned name therefore prevents success. Existing names are never adopted. Cleanup is identity-checked and nonrecursive; replacements/unknown children are preserved and set cleanup_complete=false.

This slice intentionally exports no production payload-handle accessor, reads/writes no CAS payload, applies no final manifest modes, has no commit/publish method, and does not activate hydrate/index routing. Drop is best-effort cleanup; explicit rollback is the evidence-bearing exit. Windows remains Unsupported because native destination topology is still unqualified there.

**Success criteria:** preflight representation in the exact destination, then create exactly the planned directory/file/link namespace through retained handles; reject concurrent names, substitutions and extra children; preserve exact POSIX link target text.

**Completeness criteria:** empty tree, explicit/implied directories, exact dangling link text, private temporary modes, CLOEXEC, representation-before-persistent-create ordering, late native failures, operation-created roots, concurrent-name races, cancellation, replacement identity, unknown children, root/leaf replacement, foreign root occupancy, explicit rollback and Drop fallback. ## Finding

OCI layer apply validates symlink components then uses path-based filesystem operations. An attacker can replace a checked component with a symlink between check and use. Staging uses a predictable, non-exclusive temporary directory, making adoption/race practical.

## Required contract

- Create staging exclusively with private permissions; never adopt existing path.
- Anchor operations to an opened directory descriptor.
- Resolve, create, write, delete, and hardlink descendants descriptor-relatively with no-follow semantics.
- Preserve OCI-valid opaque Unix symlink targets only once later writes cannot traverse them.
- Keep non-Unix explicit unsupported behavior where safe preservation is unavailable.

Cold review PR #241: apply.rs component check/use split; layer/mod.rs predictable staging. Manual Linux validation run 36254198267 also shows Alpine OCI import blocked pending valid absolute symlink support.

- Deterministic race/replacement probe cannot write outside staging.
- Existing path traversal, symlink-component, hardlink escape, and whiteout protections remain red under mutation.
- Valid Alpine absolute busybox link imports and hydrates unchanged on Unix.
- CI evidence on Linux; Windows remains explicit safe behavior.
